title: Transport of mixed global Hom comparisons across a commuting counit square
statement: Let f:X→Y and g:Y′→Y, X′=X×_Y Y′. Let M,N∈D(X), E∈D(X′), K∈D(Y), t:Lg_X*N→E, e:Rf_*N→K and e′:Rf′_*E→Lg*K. Assume canonical β_M is invertible and β_N followed by Rf′_*t and e′ equals Lg*e. Then the canonical pullback global Hom comparison [lem-sc-flat-affine-global-hom-comparison] at (M,N), followed by Hom(t), normalized scalar-square comparison and counit-induced global direct-image Hom(e′), equals global direct-image Hom(e), pullback comparison at (Rf_*M,K), and restricted Hom(β_M inverse,identity). Comparisons are those of [lem-sc-mixed-hom-direct-image-comparison, lem-sc-mixed-global-hom-adjunction-isIso] and the module and sheaf localization universes are independent. There are no properness, flatness, perfectness or right-adjoint hypotheses.

proof.text: Expand the pullback and direct-image Hom comparisons as evaluation mates. Transpose both paths under the canonical tensor-Hom and pullback/direct-image bijections. Expand the base-change mate as the canonical pullback composition isomorphism followed by the counit. Counit naturality and the triangle identity identify the two tensor-evaluation composites. On K-flat representatives the tensorators respect composition since both are ordinary tensor pullback; their localization equations transport the equality. Leray respects composition by uniqueness of the right-derived comparison with the same unit, giving exactly the canonical scalar square. This gives the exchange identity with β_M in the first entry and β_N in the second.

Postcompose the exchange identity by Hom of Rf′_*t followed by e′. Naturality in the second Hom entry replaces β_N followed by these arrows by Lg*e, using the assumed square. Pullback comparison naturality moves e to the source. Cancel β_M in the contravariant Hom entry, yielding Hom of its inverse and the displayed equality.
